purpose: The frozen import manifest records what arrived and never changes. This file records every authorized deviation from it: overrides of imported paths, new maintained candidate source, and known inherited defects. tools/repo-check.py rejects any drift, deletion or reclassification that is not listed here, and rejects a listed entry whose recorded hashes no longer match.
rules: An override must name the exact path, the original SHA-256 from the frozen manifest, the resulting SHA-256 on disk, a rationale, and the integration target that consumes it.
Refreshing a baseline hash to absorb a modification is prohibited. Record an override instead.
An inherited defect is registered by exact path and exact hash. If that file changes or disappears, the check FAILS rather than silently passing.
A registered inherited defect narrows to one diagnostic on one path. It never exempts a directory, and never suppresses a new defect.

A frozen path that is not in the import manifest must appear in frozen_external_records with its hash, origin and reason. Such a record may ONLY cover a path the import manifest does not already pin: it can never overwrite an import-manifest entry, because that would bless a modified imported file without an original hash, rationale or integration target. Being absent from both is a failure, not a default pass.
Reclassifying candidate source out of its scope cannot be used to skip its tests. If files are tracked under candidate/ and none is classified maintained-candidate, the run fails.

inherited_defects.evidence: The file arrived truncated in the transport pack and was imported byte-for-byte. Its hash matches the frozen import manifest, so the truncation predates this repository.
resolution_options: Recover the complete original from the restored full 604 reference and register it as an override.
Record it permanently as a truncated evidence fragment.
inherited_defects.prohibited: Do not guess the missing tail, and do not edit the original merely to make a syntax check green.

content_preserved_in.what: The truncated file itself. Lines 1-9 hold the complete request object, including the only verbatim copy of the system-prompt string; what is missing is the function's closing brace and anything that may have followed it, which cannot be known.

Enumerates every parameter in prose: predict 128, temp 0.3, reasoning_budget 0, seed 42, kvCache false, captureThinking true, the message/empty-sourceRefs schema and a bounded prior pair. It does not reproduce the system-prompt text, and its pointer to the builder does not say the builder is truncated.

The shipped implementation of the same source-free request: identical predict/temp/reasoning_budget/seed, captureThinking, schema name, maxLength 500 and maxItems 0. NOT identical: it substitutes an explicit English/Spanish for "in their language" in the system prompt, sets no kvCache flag, bounds the prior context to exactly one user/assistant pair, and adds minItems 0.

recommended_resolution.rationale: The file has no caller anywhere in the tree. Its parameters survive in REPORT.md and, with the stated differences, in shipped code; its prompt string survives in the file itself. Option 1 needs the restored 1,518,762,347-byte reference to recover what is most likely a closing brace.
recommended_resolution.correction: The audit described conversation-request.js as carrying a byte-identical system prompt. Measured on 2026-09-24 it does not: the language clause differs. Preservation is substantial, not verbatim.
recommended_resolution.status: Recommended, not adopted. Choosing option 2 forgoes recovery from the full reference, which is an owner decision. The finding stays OPEN until then.
